errors.english: arrived in that city while traveling through the lands.
errors.why: The Tibetan (and Sanskrit sukṛtaiḥ) says Vipaśyin came to the city, drawn by their good deeds (merit); that motivation is dropped.

note: A faithful verse rendering of the Anaṅgaṇa story; one small omission.

errors.english: once feigned sleep, busily watching his face. Feeling a fitting bashfulness at this, she suddenly opened her eyes and laughed.
errors.why: The prince feigns sleep while she is busy gazing at his face, and it is he who suddenly opens his eyes and laughs at her as she becomes embarrassed; the English gives both actions to her, which is incoherent.

errors.english: Sujati Noble Birth and Sucarita Noble Conduct
errors.why: brtul zhugs bzang po renders Suvrata (good vow/observance), not Sucarita, and rigs bzang po is Sujāta, so the reconstructed Sanskrit names are wrong.

note: A good literary rendering of the Sudhana episode, with one confusion over who feigned sleep and the brahmins' names wrongly reconstructed.

errors.english: "Desire" refers to what is accepted.
errors.why: 'dod pa glosses a lemma in the sense of what is held or maintained (iṣṭa), not desire.

errors.english: "actor" or "jester"
errors.why: dzab mkhan is a mutterer or chatterer (japa), someone who talks even with no listener, not an actor or jester.

errors.english: This belongs to the Victorious One
errors.why: rgyal ba can names a commentator (Jina) whose reading is cited, not the Buddha as 'the Victorious One'.

errors.english: the treatise is thereby refuted.
errors.why: The sentence continues on the next side, where 'the treatise and one's own words' are given as the parallel example; nothing says the treatise is refuted.

note: The general line of the self-refutation argument comes through, but several lemma glosses and a cited commentator's name are mistranslated.

errors.english: "She should be my wife,"
errors.why: The king's thought concerns whether she is (the ascetic's) wife; 'should be my wife' is not in the Tibetan.

note: A faithful rendering of prose and verse; the king's thought is slightly recast.

errors.english: seeing each as two-fold makes eight types of knowledge
errors.why: 'Seeing' (mthong ba) is a separate lemma of the rule, defined as the eight patiences (kṣānti); the English merges it into the definition of 'knowing'.

fix.find: likewise, for the four truths, seeing each as two-fold makes eight types of knowledge. These are the patience
fix.replace: likewise, two for each of the four truths. "Seeing" refers to the eight: the patience

errors.english: claiming, "You have power;
errors.why: The nun claims 'I have the power'.

errors.english: If she desires to appear pure
errors.why: The formula is 'wishing to be purified' (of the offence, by admitting it), not wishing to appear pure.

errors.english: The so-called human qualities [note: superhuman or superior human states]
errors.why: The commentary defines 'human dharma' as the five hindrances, and what is superior to it is the superhuman; the note conflates the two.

note: The nuns' fourth pārājika rule is rendered well, but the commentary's 'seeing' lemma is merged into 'knowing' and the claimant's 'I' becomes 'you'.
Faithful: the slander, the four hells with their durations, and the later karmic results are all accurately rendered.

errors.english: vehicle of impermanence
errors.why: stong pa nyid is emptiness: the stainless system is the vehicle of emptiness.

fix.find: belongs to the vehicle of impermanence
fix.replace: belongs to the vehicle of emptiness

errors.english: has perfectly diagnosed the entire collection of diverse things as being conceptualizations based on error
errors.why: The gloss says the Buddha designated the whole range of meanings as correct and as erroneous (the tathya/atathya teaching), i.e. expressed and taught them in words; it is not a diagnosis that all things are erroneous conceptualizations.

errors.english: By the method of definitive expression
errors.why: nges pa'i tshig is nirukti, an etymology: the clause gives the etymology of Tathāgata ('one who teaches the reality of things as it is'); it is not a separate statement about the Buddhas' method.

note: The argument is broadly followed, but emptiness becomes 'impermanence' and two glosses on the root text are misread.

errors.english: Regarding the phrase "following and reversing,"
errors.why: rjes 'gro ldog pa is anvaya-vyatireka, positive and negative concomitance, the technical term of the causal argument.

errors.english: One who remains connected to both former and latter times is not perceived through direct perception because they do not occur in sequence.
errors.why: A gloss ('the abider is the one connected with earlier and later times') is merged with the opponent's objection ('it is not perceptible because it is not sequential', marked zhes zer ba la), so the objection is presented as the author's statement.

errors.english: Even if there is a gathering, because there is no transformation, there is no contradiction
errors.why: 'du ba here is inherence (samavāya), and this clause is the start of the opponent's view that ends at snyam du sems pa la; the English renders it as 'gathering' and asserts it as the author's own view.

note: The dense Pramāṇa commentary is followed only roughly: technical terms are literalized and the opponent's views are not marked as such.

errors.english: "Mind Only" [note: the Cittamantra or Yogacara school]
errors.why: Here 'mind only' is the scriptural word ('the three realms are mind only') whose 'only' excludes primal matter as creator; the note misidentifies it as the school, and misspells it.

note: An accurate rendering of Jayānanda's lemma-by-lemma glosses on Madhyamakāvatāra 6; one misleading note.

errors.english: the possession of any goods resting upon it is established by that mat itself
errors.why: The point is that the spread mat is the 'place' (sthāna) of the goods resting on it, which matters for when they count as moved from their place; it says nothing about possession.

errors.english: Wherever even a single minute atom (paramanu) the smallest physical particle is moved
errors.why: The text says that when the whole object moves by even an atom's breadth, it has left its place; it does not say that moving a single atom of it is enough.

note: The theft rules and the variant recitation are rendered accurately on the whole, with two technical points blurred.
